about: D-34 acceptance (Mesh-LLM/capsules-plugin#69): pushes are accepted on the half's evidence key, not the sender id. Each case is a push to a receiver, its reply, and the citing record the receiver sealed when it held the half. The operator_binding cases carry the sender's binding to its operator's Nostr key (Mesh-LLM/capsules-plugin#113): the citing record seals its digest, and whether the receiver's own binding names the same operator, never the Nostr key. Test keys only.

cases.name: known_key_other_transport_id
cases.covers: a half signed by the key a host announced for node-b, pushed under another id, is held: accepted_via host_announced

tee_attestation.context: no TEE quote measured (no TDX hardware on this host, or the producer leg has not run here); recorded absent, never fabricated

binary_attestation.context: os_measured: the KERNEL (AMFI) reported this process's code-directory hash (cdhash) at exec time via csops(2) CS_OPS_CDHASH — an independent measurer beneath the process, so a compromised process cannot repoint this hash at a decoy file the way self-measurement can; the signature also binds this cdhash to the self-measured digest, so tampering with either after signing breaks verification. Trustworthy only up to: SIP enabled, a NON-ROOT attacker (root can disable SIP / bypass AMFI), and this binary's signing strength — signing_authority=unknown_local_or_ad_hoc, ad-hoc signed (no Developer-ID / notarization / library validation). Does NOT prove hardware-rooted measurement: no TEE and no hardware register are involved, so this is NOT tee_measured. A root attacker with SIP disabled is the named residual, closed only by tee_measured (out of scope here).
